title: Course Knowledge Checks
description: Interactive knowledge check questions extracted directly from the ISA/IEC 62443 course materials.

questions.question: Which statement explains the purpose of the ISA/IEC 62443 series in securing Industrial Automation and Control Systems (IACS)?

options.text: To define a universal security framework that applies exclusively to IT networks
To provide general cybersecurity guidelines that do not require industry-specific customization
To establish a structured approach to cybersecurity tailored to industrial automation and control environments
To mandate specific technologies that all industries must use to secure IACS

questions.explanation: The ISA/IEC 62443 series is specifically designed to provide a flexible, structured framework tailored to industrial automation and control environments (IACS), accounting for operational safety, availability priorities, and ICS-specific architectures rather than generic IT networks or rigid technology mandates.

questions.question: What is the role of the ISA99 Committee in developing the ISA/IEC 62443 series?

options.text: Enforces cybersecurity laws for all industrial sectors
Focuses solely on IT security and does not address industrial automation
Creates security policies for government agencies rather than private industries
Develops and maintains the ISA/IEC 62443 standards to improve IACS cybersecurity

questions.explanation: The ISA99 Committee is the international consensus-based group responsible for developing, writing, and maintaining the ISA/IEC 62443 series of standards to enhance cybersecurity across industrial automation and control systems.

questions.question: What is the primary distinction between an Industrial Control System (ICS) and an Industrial Automation and Control System (IACS) as described in ISA/IEC 62443?

options.text: IACS refers only to cybersecurity controls, while ICS includes physical safety measures
ICS is a subset of IACS, focusing mainly on hardware and software, while IACS includes people, policies, and processes
ICS focuses solely on critical infrastructure, whereas IACS applies only to manufacturing environments
IACS is exclusive to North America, while ICS is a globally recognized term

questions.explanation: An Industrial Control System (ICS) typically denotes the physical hardware, software, and control equipment, whereas an Industrial Automation and Control System (IACS) encompasses the broader socio-technical ecosystem including people, operational policies, and organizational processes.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the role of ISA/IEC 62443-3-2 in IACS cybersecurity?

options.text: Focuses on cybersecurity risk assessment and system design, helping asset owners define security zones and conduits
Provides guidelines for cloud-based security in industrial environments
Mandates encryption standards for all industrial control networks
Describes hardware specifications required for industrial cybersecurity compliance

questions.explanation: ISA/IEC 62443-3-2 provides the standard methodology for assessing cybersecurity risk, conducting risk assessments, and designing secure industrial systems through the establishment of security zones and conduits.

questions.question: Why is the ISA/IEC 62443-4-1 standard critical for securing industrial control systems?

options.text: Specifies incident response plans for industrial cybersecurity breaches
Ensures full automation of cybersecurity processes in industrial environments
Establishes requirements for a secure product development lifecycle for control system components
Mandates immediate security patching for all industrial systems without exceptions

questions.explanation: ISA/IEC 62443-4-1 defines the mandatory requirements for a secure product development lifecycle (SDLC) that product suppliers must follow when designing, developing, and maintaining industrial control components.

questions.question: According to ISA/IEC 62443, why should cybersecurity awareness be given the same emphasis as safety and operational integrity in an Industrial Automation and Control System (IACS) environment?

options.text: IT security threats do not significantly impact industrial control systems
Safety incidents are more frequent than cybersecurity incidents in industrial environments
Operational integrity is only affected by mechanical failures, not cybersecurity threats
Cybersecurity failures can directly lead to physical safety risks and operational disruptions

questions.explanation: In operational technology and IACS, cybersecurity incidents are not just data breaches—they can cause physical harm to personnel, environmental disasters, and catastrophic operational disruptions.

questions.question: According to best practices in ISA/IEC 62443 which of the following would best ensure the effectiveness of a cybersecurity awareness programme for employees of a manufacturing company?

options.text: Conducting a single, large-scale awareness session once a year for all employees
Customising awareness activities based on employee roles and responsibilities
Providing technical training only to IT staff, since they handle cybersecurity
Making cybersecurity training optional to avoid interfering with daily operations

questions.explanation: Effective security awareness must be role-based. Operators, engineers, plant managers, and IT personnel face different threat vectors and require customized awareness programs tailored to their specific responsibilities.

questions.question: A power grid operator wants to demonstrate the impact of cyber threats on industrial control systems to increase awareness. According to Section 2, which of the following best aligns with this goal?

options.text: Disabling network access for employees who fail cybersecurity tests
Conducting an employee satisfaction survey about cybersecurity training
Requiring all staff to read cybersecurity policy documents without additional engagement
Showing a demonstration of Industroyer malware on a protection relay

questions.explanation: Demonstrating real-world industrial malware (such as Industroyer which targeted Ukrainian power substations) on test equipment or through controlled demonstrations provides tangible, high-impact awareness for operations staff.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes why security awareness must be an ongoing process rather than a one-time activity?

options.text: Awareness programmes should only be conducted during security breaches
Employees tend to ignore cybersecurity policies, so frequent reminders enforce compliance
Cyber threats are constantly evolving, requiring regular updates to knowledge and behaviour
Once trained, employees do not require additional cybersecurity education

questions.explanation: Threat actors, phishing techniques, and industrial attack vectors evolve continuously. Ongoing awareness ensures staff maintain vigilance and adapt to emerging threats.

questions.question: A company wants to raise cybersecurity awareness at the executive level. According to best practices in ISA/IEC 62443, which solution best addresses this need?

options.text: Organising Board Member sessions that reveal high-impact cybersecurity risks
Sending a monthly cybersecurity newsletter to all employees, including executives
Assigning technical cybersecurity training to board members
Restricting executive access to sensitive cybersecurity information

questions.explanation: Executives and board members require high-level briefings focused on business risk, operational resilience, and liability rather than technical configuration details.
